findings.title: Codec group can outlive outer FIRST CPU timeout
findings.detail: Each codec starts a separate session/process group and communicate waits85seconds. The pinned outer CPU supervisor also times out at85seconds and cleans only its Python child group. If the outer limit expires before convert finally runs, the separate codec group escapes outer cleanup;CPU30does not bound a sleeping/stalled child wall time. This can occur even with a shorter per-convert timeout when conversion starts late in the suite. Current timeout test mocks Popen and cannot verify this outer-timeout closure.
findings.recommendation: For bounded CPU controls keep spawned codec children in the outer owned group,or explicitly register and close their groups from the outer supervisor. Preserve production ownership cleanup separately. Add a real short outer-timeout regression proving the spawned converter is gone.
